posts.text:
Scott Hanson of NFL RedZone used to EDIT Jesus OUT of a coach’s interviews. That same coach led him to the Lord.

“Every time I would interview him, he would say something about Jesus. I wasn’t hostile, but I used to edit it out. I never put that on television.”

“It turned out Ken Leonard was and is a Bible-believing, born-again Christian who was awesome as a football coach, but he used that as a platform to impact others and glorify God. And he led me to the Lord.”

“On April 23, 1996, I understood: 
• I was a sinner in need of a savior.
• Sin has a penalty.
• Christ paid the penalty.
• Salvation is a free gift. I didn’t earn it.
• I must receive the one whose name is above all other names.”  

“There was no lightning bolt that hit me at that moment. But the Bible tells me several things happened:
• A dead man came alive.
• The Holy Spirit started planting love, joy, peace, patience, and kindness.
• Angels in heaven rejoiced because God had done it again.”

That coach must have watched those interviews on TV and seen how they were edited, but he kept giving Jesus the credit. 

Never underestimate what God can do with a faithful witness.

posts.text:
"They need approval to eat. Oftentimes they'll eat out of dog bowls." That's a husband talking about his wife and his two live-in girlfriends. He tracks all three through their phones, their watches and their cars, reads every message they send and won't let them on his couch:

His name is Scott. All three women call him Daddy. His wife Brenda has been with him for over ten years, married for nine, and they talked about bringing in other women from the very start. Samantha met him at work seven years ago. Aydriana found him online in October 2023. He was her first real relationship.

Then came the contract. Wake-up times, outfits, rules, punishments, all written down. Scott says they usually sign it in blood. Even one of the women admits the blood part is a little extra. Another didn't even blink:

"I'm here to serve him and that's part of my service."

Every outfit gets his approval. Leaving the house takes permission, and so does coming home. No social media unless he signs off on it. He calls the women an extension of him. They call it safety.

"I don't worry about losing my independence."

Instead of wedding rings, they wear collars he designed himself. Asked what means more, a ring or a collar, one of them doesn't think twice:

"For me, it's the collar."

The comment they get most online is that none of the women have safewords or limits. Strangers call it irresponsible. Old friends and family walked away. Scott's answer about the girls sitting on the floor:

"They enjoy it, I enjoy it, so what's the issue?"

His oldest friend Gwen sat them all down at dinner and asked why anyone would hand a man that much control. One of the girls answered first:

"He can direct my life better than I can."

Another said she grew up with no structure and no dad. Three women, one man, no safewords. And a contract signed in blood.

$SPX: I Called for a Selloff Weeks Ago. Now 8,100 or the Ultimate Bull Trap? | November 11, 2026 | Elliott Wave Update 🚨

Back on October 17, I shared my $SPX / SP500 Elliott Wave outlook, anticipating another corrective move into a predefined buy zone before a potential final bullish impulse.

Three weeks later, SPX dropped almost exactly into that region around 7,350 and has since staged a sharp recovery toward 7,630.

The original roadmap has played out remarkably well so far. But hitting the projected downside target was only the first part of the equation. The more interesting question now is whether we have actually completed Wave (4) and are heading into the final bullish Wave (5), or whether this recovery is setting up a larger bull trap.

I'm currently tracking two scenarios, with the bullish interpretation remaining my preferred count.

---
SCENARIO 1: Expanded Flat Completed — Next Stop 8,100+?
---

My original thesis was that the correction from the August high would unfold as an Expanded Flat (3-3-5), forming Wave (4) within the larger Wave III.

The initial decline into September established Wave A near 7,484, followed by a corrective Wave B rally into October that marginally exceeded the August high. The subsequent selloff then delivered the anticipated Wave C, reaching our predefined Fibonacci buy zone around 7,350.

The price relationships fit the Expanded Flat interpretation, although the internal 3-3-5 subdivisions still require confirmation.

What makes the current situation particularly interesting is the reaction from that support region. SPX has recovered sharply, raising the possibility that Wave (4) terminated at the November low.

If that's the case, we should now be entering the early stages of Wave (5).

My preferred path would be an initial Wave (i) advance toward 7,640–7,660, followed by a corrective Wave (ii) pullback into approximately 7,456–7,539. From there, a stronger Wave (iii) could develop toward 7,919–8,000, eventually followed by Waves (iv) and (v), completing the larger Wave III around 8,080–8,129.

The previous ATH at 7,844.52 will be the critical upside confirmation level. A sustained breakout would significantly strengthen this interpretation.

For now, the November low around 7,350 is the key structural reference. A move below it would invalidate the proposed impulsive Wave (5) beginning from that low.

Of course, the Fibonacci targets will need recalculation once the actual Wave (i) and (ii) endpoints are established.

---
SCENARIO 2: October Was the Top — Another Decline Toward 7,000?
---

There is still a legitimate bearish alternative.

In this interpretation, the October high at 7,844.52 marked the completion of the larger five-wave advance. The subsequent selloff would therefore represent the beginning of a higher-degree ABC correction rather than a temporary Wave (4).

The first decline into 7,349 could be Wave A, while the current recovery would represent a corrective Wave B.

That would make the 7,675–7,739 region particularly interesting as potential resistance, with additional resistance extending toward 7,772.

If SPX stalls in that area and subsequently resumes its decline, a final Wave C could target the former ATH from early 2026 around 7,002, with a broader potential termination zone between 6,883 and 7,040.

I find this alternative worth monitoring because the former ATH provides a clearly defined structural support reference. Whether it also becomes a Fibonacci confluence zone will depend on where Wave B ultimately terminates.

One important adjustment to my earlier bearish count: I would no longer rely on the proposed Ending Diagonal as a confirmed pattern. Its required internal structure and Wave 1–4 overlap have not been sufficiently established. The broader completed-top scenario can still be considered without forcing that specific formation.

A sustained breakout above 7,844.52 would invalidate the hypothesis that October marked the final high.

SO WHICH SCENARIIO HAS THE EDGE?

For now, I continue to favor the bullish Expanded Flat interpretation.

We identified the potential correction and its target region weeks before the selloff occurred. SPX subsequently reached that region and delivered the anticipated reversal reaction.

That's encouraging, but it doesn't automatically confirm that the correction is finished.

The next important clue will come from the internal structure of the recovery. If SPX develops five impulsive waves higher, followed by a corrective three-wave pullback, the bullish case gains credibility. If the rebound instead unfolds as a corrective ABC and fails below the October high, the bearish alternative becomes increasingly relevant.

My preferred roadmap remains a continuation toward 8,100+, while the alternative points to another corrective decline toward the former ATH around 7,000.

Both scenarios are now clearly defined, including their respective confirmation and invalidation levels.

Predicting the exact future path isn't the objective. The value of Elliott Wave analysis lies in identifying potential market structures, price targets and invalidation levels before the moves unfold.

The first part of my October roadmap has materialized. Now we'll see whether the market delivers the second. 

AND ONE FINAL OBERVATION:

Whenever the market makes a significant move, the usual crowd of so-called stock market experts suddenly appears with detailed explanations of why it happened. Macroeconomics, sentiment, historical comparisons, and the inevitable Warren Buffett quotes.

Yet remarkably few seem willing to publish concrete scenarios, price targets, and invalidation levels weeks before the actual move.

"Explaining yesterday's price action is easy." 

Anticipating tomorrow's possibilities, putting your analysis on record, and accepting the risk of being wrong — that's where real market analysis begins!
